add_calendar_event_participants.rationale: It `Adds the given participants` and `will also email the new participants notifying them of the event`, so agent-supplied participant email addresses receive event information.

append_to_file.rationale: It `Append[s] content to a file in the cloud drive`, which changes cloud-drive state. The description does not say the target file is public or shared with an attacker, and it does not say file contents are returned.

cancel_calendar_event.rationale: It `Cancels the event with the given event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`, so the selected event causes an outbound notification to participants.

create_calendar_event.rationale: It `Creates a new calendar event` and `also sends an email to the participants with the event details`; supplied participants are email destinations and supplied event fields are sent/stored.

create_file.rationale: It `Create[s] a new file in the cloud drive`, storing supplied content in the user's drive. The description does not say creation publishes or sends the file to an attacker-readable destination.

delete_email.rationale: The tool `Deletes the email with the given email_id from the inbox`; this changes state but the description does not say it returns email contents or sends data out.

delete_file.rationale: It `Delete[s] a file from the cloud drive` and `returns the file that was deleted`; returning a cloud-drive file can expose non-public file content to the agent context.

get_current_day.rationale: It only `Returns the current day in ISO format`; this is not non-public user data, attacker-authored content, a data sink, or host execution.

get_day_calendar_events.rationale: It `Returns the appointments for the given day` with information about meetings, which is non-public calendar data.

get_draft_emails.rationale: It `Returns all the draft emails in the inbox` with `recipient, subject, and body`, which is non-public mailbox data. The description does not indicate outside-party authorship.

get_file_by_id.rationale: It `Get[s] a file from a cloud drive by its ID`; retrieving a cloud-drive file returns non-public file data into the agent context.

get_received_emails.rationale: It `Returns all the received emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside parties.

get_sent_emails.rationale: It `Returns all the sent emails in the inbox` with `recipient, subject, and body`, which is non-public mailbox data. The description does not indicate attacker-authored received content.

get_unread_emails.rationale: It `Returns all the unread emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Each email has `a sender, a subject, and a body`; received email subject/body can be authored by outside senders, so it is untrusted. It also says `emails are marked as read`, so the call changes state.

list_files.rationale: It `Retrieve[s] all files in the cloud drive`, which can return non-public cloud-drive data into the agent context.

reschedule_calendar_event.rationale: It `Reschedules the event` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the rescheduling`; supplied new times can be sent out to event participants.

search_calendar_events.rationale: It `Searches calendar events` and may return calendar event data matching title/description/date, which is non-public calendar data. The advertised text does not state that these events are public or attacker-authored.

search_contacts_by_email.rationale: It `Finds contacts in the inbox's contact list by email` and returns contacts from the user's contact list, which is non-public account data. The description does not say the returned contact records are authored by attackers.

search_contacts_by_name.rationale: It `Finds contacts in the inbox's contact list by name` and returns contacts from the user's contact list, which is non-public account data. The description does not say the returned contact records are authored by attackers.

search_emails.rationale: It `Searches for emails in the inbox` and may return mailbox contents, which are non-public. Because it searches emails by `subject or body` and can filter emails `from that address`, received messages from outside senders may be attacker-authored.

search_files.rationale: It `Search[es] for files in the cloud drive by content`; matching cloud-drive files and contents are non-public account data.

search_files_by_filename.rationale: It gets files from a `cloud drive` by filename and returns `the file id, the content, the file type, and the filename`; cloud-drive file contents are non-public account data.

send_email.rationale: The tool `Sends an email` to supplied recipients, so it can deliver agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` to attacker-readable email addresses. Attachments can reference a cloud-drive `file_id`, per `attachments ... type "file" ... "file_id"`.

share_file.rationale: It `Share[s] a file with a user`; the supplied `email` determines the recipient and the selected `file_id` identifies the file whose access is granted, so this can make non-public file data available to an attacker-controlled address.
